Definition: Does the register cover births, deaths and marriages?
Comments: Covers live births, deaths, foetal deaths, marriage, separation, divorce, annulment, adoption, legitimation, recognition per revised Family Code Law no 16/008 (2016).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed against the primary legal text: Family Code Law 16/008 (15 July 2016, leganet.cd) establishes a distinct civil status register recording all births, marriages and deaths, and the UNECA APAI-CRVS snapshot corroborates that the recast law provides the legislative framework for live births, deaths, foetal deaths, marriages, separations and related acts. Value Code 3 (All) is well supported by an authoritative primary source, not just the single snapshot originally cited.

Definition: Does the government maintain a digital electoral register?
Comments: Digital biometric electoral register; 46.7M voters deduplicated with fingerprints/face in 2018 by CENI using MegaMatcher ABIS.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with fresher, independent evidence: CENI's biometric voter register (ABIS-based) was externally audited in May 2023, validating 43,955,181 of 47,299,364 raw enrolments across the 26 provinces. Enrolment could not be completed in Kwamouth, Masisi, Nyiragongo, Rutshuru and part of Maluku due to insecurity, so the register is near-nationwide but not complete. Value Code 4 (Partially deployed) upheld, replacing the outdated single 2018 vendor case study with 2023 CENI/media sources.

Definition: What proportion of the electorate does the register cover?
Comments: 46.7M registered voters; population ~80-90M, eligible ~40-50M, suggests 70-89% coverage after dedup.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Updated with 2023 CENI audit data: 43,955,181 validated voters against an expected/eligible electorate of 49,283,109 (CENI, 2023) is approximately 89% coverage, sitting right on the boundary between the 70-89% and >89% bands. Given uncertainty in the eligible-population denominator, retained Value Code 4 (70-89%) rather than upgrading on a single ratio calculation — flagged for human review to confirm whether a firmer eligible-population estimate would push this into the >89% band.

Definition: Does the government maintain a separate cadastral register?
Comments: Separate cadastral planned for digitization under e-Foncier.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The 2022 PPP with eProseed (which was to deliver a pilot digitised title in the Gombe circumscription by December 2022) appears to have stalled: as of February 2025 the government reports no update on its progress and is instead negotiating a new partner (Oxinus, blockchain-based proposal) to build e-Foncier, with no agreement yet signed. No evidence of an operating separate digital cadastral register was found. Value Code revised down from 3 (Under development) to 2 (Planned), since the digitisation effort has reverted to the planning/negotiation stage rather than active technical development.

Definition: Does the government maintain one or more tax registers?
Comments: Digital tax registers via DGI; online registration, e-invoicing (Facture Normalisee phase 1 2024), DGI Mobile app.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and updated with primary DGI sources: mandatory e-invoicing (facture normalisée via e-DEF/e-UF/e-MCF electronic fiscal devices) for VAT-registered taxpayers took effect nationwide on 1 December 2025, following a phased rollout since 2024, and DGI operates online taxpayer registration/e-filing platforms (edef.dgirdc.cd). Coverage remains partial (VAT-liable taxpayers with turnover above the threshold, not the full income-tax base), so Value Code 4 (Partially deployed) is upheld with substantially more current and authoritative sourcing than the single Sovos blog post originally cited.
